items.title: Vince Giordano interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: The interviewer mentions Pee Wee Russell in the context of Kenny Dorham's experience; the interviewee responds generally about the value of seeing musicians 'in the flesh' and refers to 'those three aforementioned reed players of my time' without explicitly stating he personally met or played with P

ctx.x: I mean that’s what Kenny, when he talked about Adrian Rollini and hearing Pee Wee Russell, that changed his life you know.

To be in the flesh. I think you know there’s a lot of musicians today that they look at these things as historical things but there’s no one-on-one, there’s no contact. It’s — all right some of the films have been coming out and you can go on YouTube and watch an occasional great jazz performance, but it’s not the same as going to a club and seeing them, and aww damn it, I played that solo bad, or spit on the floor or spill over a drink or whatever. I mean these guys were gods. And those three aforementioned reed…
